Ruling: batch #152 item 3 · letter 1 (Part 1 only — repair the two dormant closing-keyword sites in `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` and pin them with seeded tables; ⛔ Part 2's differential emitter gate is not built) · maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-09-18T03:58Z

Director seat, summon #24, `session_01Wj1HUjzyeiBQ8atRf1ZhaL`. Presented in detail with the recommendation **1**; the maintainer agreed. Facts (this card; triage 5716033545): `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` spells a GitHub closing keyword immediately before an interpolated anchor at two stale-entry sites — one a byte-identical twin of the tail objectui#9595 replaced; both ledgers (`DEBT`, `TEST_DEBT`) are empty today, so both sites are dormant, one ledger entry from rendering. The gate exports its collector and audit, so a rendered pin can drive them with seeded tables directly. Part 2 asked for a differential, branch-scoped gate over every text emitted by `scripts/` — a fourth one-at-a-time repair in this family (objectui#9535, #9595, #9597).

## Ruling — **1**

- Part 1 lands: both sites repaired in the shape objectui#9595 used, one rendered pin per site driven through the exported collector/audit with seeded ledger rows (red on the current head, green after).
- ⛔ **Part 2** — a new required gate is the human floor and the maintainer's standing direction is no further gate development; if the shape appears a fifth time, that occurrence is the evidence for a card, ⛔ not this one.
- objectui#9597 (live: non-empty ledger, open anchor) stays graded above this and is queued separately.

Four-facet reading: ① zero customers; ② one shape, one fix, no new instrument; ③ not scored — fleet-facing; ④ nothing added.

## Execution

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:ui`, `priority:p2`, `tooling` stay.

The dispatch order carries that as an absolute, because triage predicted the exact failure: 「若照原样入队,后果是可预见的:承接的 dev 会连着 Part 2 一起建一道新门禁」.

## Re-derived on the tree before dispatch, ⛔ not adopted from the card

`main` = `4b57722997a4ebfb1dfd03a21a3c9b654264efd9`.

**The two sites.** ⚠️ The card warns that a single-line `git grep` under-counts this family because `check-action-forward-parity.mjs` splits its sentence across concatenated chunks. So I ran the collapsed instrument as primary — strip `" + "` / `' + '` / backtick concatenation and `\n` escapes, then match a closing keyword immediately before an interpolated anchor — and the naive grep only as a control:

| instrument | reading |
|:--|:--|
| collapsed text | **2** |
| naive single-line grep | **2** |

They agree, at `:508` and `:751`. ⇒ worth saying plainly so the next reader does not spend the effort I did: **the concatenation trap is `check-action-forward-parity.mjs`'s, not this file's.** Both sites here sit on one line each.

```
:508   `${debt[name].issue ? ` (and close #${debt[name].issue} if it is done)` : ""}.`
:751   `${spec.issue  ? ` (and close #${spec.issue} if the list is empty)` : ""}.`
```

**Both ledgers are empty ⇒ dormant, confirmed.** `:79` `export const DEBT = {};` and `:155` `export const TEST_DEBT = {};`. ⚠️ Recording my own instrument failure rather than the reading alone: my first probe was a regex for a multi-line `const NAME = {\n … \n};` block and it printed *"block NOT FOUND"* for both. That was the regex's answer, not the tree's — the declarations are single-line. The `^export ` listing is the lit reading. ⛔ Dormant is not fixed: one ledger entry away from rendering.

**The card's 「cheaper to pin」 claim holds.** `:355` `export function collect(…)` and `:479` `export function auditPackages(packages, tables = {})` — the audit takes a `tables` parameter, so a rendered pin can drive it with seeded ledger rows directly. ⛔ No copy-the-gate-into-a-throwaway-workspace harness is needed here.

**Two landed precedents to copy, not invent.** The replacement spelling is already on `main` from this lane's own work: `check-action-forward-parity.mjs:1061`/`:1069` now read `(and objectui#${meta.issue} …` — the closing keyword removed, the anchor still interpolated. Their pins are `scripts/__tests__/check-action-forward-parity-closing-keyword.test.ts` and `scripts/__tests__/check-lint-coverage-closing-keyword.test.ts`.

## ⛔ One adjacency the dev must NOT widen into

Both sites are written as `${X.issue ? … : ""}` — the same falsy-anchor guard shape objectui#9596 is about, dispatched from this seat an hour ago. ⛔ Different question, ⛔ different card, ⛔ not folded in: there `X` is a module-level anchor constant, here it is a per-entry field on a ledger row, and both ledgers are empty. The dispatch order says so explicitly.

## Why `Clause-②: no`

Surface is `scripts/` and `scripts/__tests__/`. Path control: `packages/types/` **0**, `packages/spec/` **0**, `skills/` **0**. ⛔ No carrier hung, ⛔ none owed — and the ruling's own execution段 left `domain:ui`, `priority:p2`, `tooling` in place with nothing else added.

⛔ Not claiming on this comment: the order goes to a `mode:subagent` dev on the branch above, and the seat re-reads CI and mergeability at the landing flip.

## ACCEPT — in-seat, at the default tier

`domain:ui` execution seat, `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`, 2026-09-18T14:15Z. PR objectui#9898, head `b95a9608e`. ⛔ Not landing on this comment: I re-read CI and mergeability at the flip.

## ⛔ The fence first, because the ruling is the reason this card was dispatchable at all

The maintainer authorised Part 1 and ⛔ refused Part 2's differential emitter gate — 「a new required gate is the human floor」. Measured on the PR's own file list, by STATUS rather than by name:

```
ADDED files                                   1  → scripts/__tests__/check-type-check-coverage-closing-keyword.test.ts
ADDED gate entry points (scripts/check-*.mjs) 0
package.json touched                          0
.github/** touched                            0
files outside scripts/                        0
total files                                   2
```

⚠️ Recording an instrument failure of my own rather than only the reading: my first probe matched `^scripts/check-[^/]+\.mjs$` over ALL changed files and fired on `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` — which is the existing gate, MODIFIED. The probe ignored `status`. The corrected probe, restricted to `status == 'added'`, reads **0**. A name-shaped probe cannot answer a question about what is NEW.

⇒ the fence held. One added test in an existing suite; ⛔ no new gate, ⛔ no `check:*` registration, ⛔ no workflow.

## The repair

Both emitters converted to the landed house form — closing keyword out, anchor still interpolated and now qualified:

```
:508   … so the gap cannot reopen` + `${debt[name].issue ? `, and objectui#${debt[name].issue} can be ended once that work is done` : ""}.`
:778   … so the gap cannot reopen` + `${spec.issue     ? `, and objectui#${spec.issue} can be ended once the list is empty` : ""}.`
```

Matching `check-lint-coverage.mjs` and `check-action-forward-parity.mjs`, ⛔ not a fourth invented spelling. A banner sits at each ratchet stating the rule and — correctly — citing the precedents **by the names of the things rather than by line address**, per root `AGENTS.md` commandment #11. The banner also says the thing that actually matters and that I would have accepted a weaker version of: an empty ledger is ⛔ not a defence, it is the REASON the shape survived, because a message no entry makes reachable is read by nobody and the entry that reopens it is written by whoever will need to quote it.

## ⭐ The finding that corrects MY dispatch order, not the dev's work

I told the dev my two instruments agreed at **2**, and framed that agreement as a control. It was not one. Re-measured in this seat, with the `CLOSING_TRIGGER` regex the four landed pins in this family share byte-for-byte — which also accepts a LITERAL anchor and an `owner/repo` | `objectui` | `objectstack` qualifier:

| instrument | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| my order's rule (keyword + **interpolated** anchor) | 2 | 0 |
| the landed pins' own `CLOSING_TRIGGER` | **3** | **1** |

The extra hit, before and after, is `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs:128`:

```
//     input surface (`z.input`), the fix objectstack#4074 applied in `types`.
```

⇒ the NOUN `fix` in "the fix … applied", inside a source comment. ⛔ Not an emitter, never reaches a rendered diagnostic, and a `.mjs` comment is not a surface GitHub parses for closing grammar in the first place. Leaving it is right, and matches what objectui#9755's author recorded as shape-only, lowest severity.

**The lesson is mine and it is the shift's recurring one.** My "collapsed instrument plus grep control, both read 2" was two instruments sharing one assumption — that the anchor is interpolated. Agreement between instruments that share a premise is not a control; it is the same reading twice. The repo already had the wider rule, written into four pins, and my order quoted a narrower one at the dev. The dev measured the fence instead of obeying it, which is exactly what I asked for.

⚠️ Second, smaller: my claim comment's quote of site 2 carries two spaces before the `?`; the tree has one. I inserted it to align a code block. A block presented as a tree reading may ⛔ not be prettified — that is a fabricated byte in a quotation, however harmless, and the dev was right to name it.

## Two more carried out, ⛔ neither folded in

1. **A stale present-tense banner in a file this branch does not touch.** `scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs`'s DEBT ratchet says the same shape STILL STANDS in `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` and `check-action-forward-parity.mjs`. objectui#9755 falsified half of that sentence; this branch falsifies the other half. ⛔ Correctly not reshaped here — it is also readable as a historical note about what PR objectui#9595 chose not to reach. I will carry it rather than widen this PR.
2. **The concatenation trap is confirmed absent from this file** by a third, looser probe (any keyword within 40 characters of any `#` in the collapsed text) → 3 before, the same three sites. ⇒ the trap is `check-action-forward-parity.mjs`'s, as my order said, and now that is measured by three instruments rather than asserted by two.

## Verification I am relying on, and what I did ⛔ not re-run

The pin was proved red on the pre-repair gate and green after, with the substitution proved by `git hash-object` against the merge-base blob and by marker counts flipping BEFORE anything ran — ⛔ not by an exit code alone — and the restore proved by state (`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` with `HEAD` named explicitly, on-disk hash back, `git diff HEAD` empty). That is the right shape and it is the shape that has failed elsewhere this week when a bare `git checkout -- PATH` restored the mutation out of the index at exit 0. ⚠️ I did ⛔ not re-run the suites; CI is my instrument for that and it is read at the flip.

⇒ **ACCEPT.** Landing when CI converges.
